finding: The old frozen numeric width constrained the forequarters and paws to about100 native units, while the sheet suggests about140 at a common height. The body and stance read too narrow. New target is the existing drawing, not the old specification.

The previous station-loft skull lacks the broad temple/zygomatic structure, lowered nasal bridge and integrated brow hierarchy. Eye and cheek overlay planes do not create convincing underlying facial anatomy.
The mesh projects a long generic wedge with a shallow underside. The drawing has a blunt faceted nose, broader plane changes and a higher, stronger mandibular corner.

Small flat amber patches sit on a generic side surface. The reference has deep dark sockets under a heavy oblique brow with a distinct focused expression. Geometry must establish the orbit before color.
The drawing has substantially thicker deltoid/triceps masses and wrists, shorter-looking lower forelegs and a wider grounded stance. The mesh has thin elongated stick-like distal segments.
The mesh throat/chest is a rounded undifferentiated mass and the underside mask a broad tan region. The drawing separates an angular throat, deep narrow sternum and scapular/chest volumes.

The old body remains a generic smooth quadruped profile; lateral volume and lumbar curvature do not reproduce the drawing. The sheet varies between views; a coherent measured ribcage/waist/pelvis framework is needed.

The reference has strong forward knee, tight angular hock and distinct thigh-to-calf transitions. The previous body union softens those features and the posed near/far foot locations differ from the side drawing.

Counts are correct in the previous mesh but paws are too small and uniform. The art shows broad weight-bearing toe lobes, distinct knuckles and thick curved claws; the mesh reads as narrow pads with pale spikes.

The previous long horn rises too vertically and its numeric laterality conflicts with the sheet. The accepted image shows a more backward-swept long horn, visible bands, broad chipped stump and taller sharply folded ears. The new coordinate convention will honor drawn laterality.

The previous interior-sampled shields avoid major intersections but lack the broad layered wrap, strongly shaped shoulder caps and coherent peaked rear shingle silhouette. They remain plain generic plates.

The old frozen low tip was deliberately used instead of the concept arc. The new canonical sheet shows a longer raised curl; rear and side arcs still conflict and require a recorded spatial interpretation.
The mesh has broad profile planes and arbitrary fusion triangles rather than designed cheek, scapular, muscle and armor planes. Add form-driven topology before surface microdetail.

Eight broad face colors omit the reference hide-plane variation, warm anatomical underside and deliberate rusty plate margins. Painted highlights must not be mistaken for geometry; native color refinement comes after shape.
